solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Simple life forms in endless danger with measure of acidity and variable weight

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter of the word for danger is lopped off

parts.note: a synonym for danger
pH is the scale chemists use for acidity
algebra names its unknowns x, y and z
a ton is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: A biology note about primitive organisms threatened by acid and by shifting loads.
explanation.walkthrough: PERI(L) plus PH, Y and TON give PERIPHYTON.
explanation.definitionFit: Periphyton is the slimy community of algae and microbes attached to submerged surfaces, all very basic organisms.

clue.text: Lighter article being transported with baby, perhaps

indicators.note: something carried along inside a vehicle sits within it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a baby, for example, rides in a pram
the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone pushing a pram finds it lighter once an item is loaded with the baby.
explanation.walkthrough: A goes inside PRAM to give PRAAM. 'Lighter' looks like a comparison of weight but is the noun for a cargo barge.
explanation.definitionFit: A praam is a flat-bottomed boat used to ferry cargo to and from ships, which is exactly what a lighter does.

clue.text: Part of church constructed to order without elevated blocks

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting a word up makes it read from bottom to top
to block something is to sit in its way, so one piece is lodged inside the other
something constructed is built up from its parts, so those letters are put together afresh

parts.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged
w/o is the written shorthand for without

explanation.surface: A church extension is built to order, but without the raised blocks of stone it needs.
explanation.walkthrough: W/O is the written shorthand for without; in a down clue, elevating it turns it upside down before it is lodged inside the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: A rood-tower is a tower over the crossing of a church, where the rood or great crucifix stands.

clue.text: Light source left hood of palmtop damaged

indicators.note: something damaged is knocked out of shape, so these letters lose their order

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for left
taken as written

explanation.surface: A screen light on a handheld computer was left broken when its cover was damaged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks like part of the story of breakage, but it only supplies L to join the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: A photoflood lamp is a very bright tungsten bulb used by photographers to light a scene.

clue.text: Jade completely, at last appearing at station with energy falling

indicators.note: at last asks for the final letter of the word completely

parts.note: its final letter

indicators.note: in a down clue the E for energy drops from the top of the station's name to its foot

parts.note: Euston is a main-line railway terminus in London

explanation.surface: A tired traveller is utterly jaded, finally turning up at a railway station as their energy fails.
explanation.walkthrough: Jade is the noun, the stone, not the verb meaning to tire. 'at last' takes Y from completely; 'with energy falling' drops the E of EUSTON, a London rail terminus, to the foot, giving USTONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Yu-stone is the Chinese name for the precious green mineral jade, so the two name the same gemstone.

clue.text: Image capturing strike beneath circle of snake admirers

indicators.note: in a down clue, lying beneath something means coming after it in the column

parts.note: a circle is shaped like the letter O

indicators.note: to capture is to take hold of and keep inside, so one piece is held within the other

parts.note: pic is short for picture
a synonym for strike

explanation.surface: A photograph of a cult of snake-worshippers catches one of them lashing out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Circle' sits at the top of the column because 'beneath' puts the rest under it, as only a down clue can.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ophites were an early sect who revered the serpent, so ophitic describes those worshippers.

clue.text: Mountain agents blowing cover of doctor?

indicators.note: blowing the cover strips the agency's outside letters, which together spell the doctor's MD abbreviation

parts.note: Mossad is Israel's intelligence agency

explanation.surface: Secret agents expose a doctor who was working undercover.
explanation.walkthrough: The outer letters of MOSSAD, the Israeli secret service, are M and D, which is MD, a doctor: hence the question mark. 'blowing cover of' strips them away.
explanation.definitionFit: Ossa is a peak in Thessaly, Greece, famous from the myth of the giants piling it on Pelion.

clue.text: Son wanting someone else's mustard now unused

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son
envy is wanting what another person has

explanation.surface: A son covets another person's jar of mustard that is sitting there unopened.
explanation.definitionFit: Senvy is an obsolete English word for the mustard plant or its seed, no longer in ordinary use.

clue.text: War cries prepared with one inside? Man's upset

parts.note: à la, as in a menu dish prepared with or in the style of something
an old lag is a convict, someone inside prison

indicators.note: in a down clue, upsetting a word turns it upside down so it reads bottom to top

parts.note: IOM is the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: Battle shouts are readied with someone hidden within, and a man is distressed.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags 'one inside' as a prisoner, and the ’s of Man’s stands for 'is'. Menus use the French à la for a dish prepared with something.
explanation.definitionFit: Alalagmoi is the Greek plural for battle shouts, the alala cry raised by soldiers going into combat.

clue.text: Poland's ready to axe its airline travel department: airlines collectively "spineless creatures"

indicators.note: axing something cuts it out, so the named piece is removed from the longer word

parts.note: the zloty is the Polish currency, and ready is slang for cash
LOT is the Polish national airline
a synonym for travel
a branch is a department of an organisation
IATA is the International Air Transport Association

explanation.surface: Poland's government is ready to shut down its national carrier and its travel office, a cowardly move by the airlines.
explanation.walkthrough: ZLOTY loses LOT to leave ZY. 'Ready' as slang for money is British.
explanation.definitionFit: Zygobranchiata is an old zoological grouping of sea snails such as limpets and abalones, molluscs which lack backbones.

clue.text: Having no issue with answer, fine to interrupt as far as we're concerned

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for answer

indicators.note: something that interrupts breaks in between, so it lodges inside the other words

parts.note: to us, meaning in our view
OK means fine

explanation.surface: A complaint with no problem: the answer's fine, so don't interrupt, as far as we are concerned.
explanation.walkthrough: OK breaks into TO US between T and O: A + T(OK)O US. 'Issue' means children here, not a problem.
explanation.definitionFit: Atokous means childless, and issue is the legal word for offspring, so having none fits.

clue.text: Note from Donbas personnel, five years back (New York area)

parts.note: HR is human resources, the personnel department

indicators.note: going back means these two pieces are read in the opposite order

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five
Y is the abbreviation for years
the usual abbreviation
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A memo from staff in eastern Ukraine, dated five years ago, mentions New York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' looks like a message but means a banknote; Donbas is the eastern region of Ukraine.
explanation.definitionFit: The hryvnya is the currency of Ukraine, so its banknotes circulate in Donbas.

clue.text: Story maker's motto ruined with hype

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked out of its proper form, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A writer's guiding slogan has been spoilt by overblown publicity.
explanation.definitionFit: A mythopoet is a maker of myths, someone who creates legends and fables.

clue.text: Grasses turning in sleazy rozzers

indicators.note: turning round means those concealed letters run right to left
in says the letters lie inside the following words

parts.note: the letters straddle the two words

explanation.surface: Seedy police officers are switching sides over grass, as in cannabis.
explanation.walkthrough: Rozzers is British slang for police officers; 'grasses' also hints at informers.
explanation.definitionFit: Oryza is the genus of grasses that includes rice, so its members are grasses.

clue.text: Fossil fuel to be found around wide swamp down under

indicators.note: around means one piece wraps about the other

parts.note: coal is a fossil fuel
W is the cricket abbreviation for a wide

explanation.surface: Coal deposits are found all round a broad Australian marsh.
explanation.walkthrough: Down under is Australia, which flags that the definition is an Australian word.
explanation.definitionFit: Cowal is an Australian word for a swamp or shallow lake, so a marsh in Australia.

clue.text: Injured cycling in company with students, one went on foot

indicators.note: cycling sends the last letter of the word round to the front

parts.note: injured means hurt
NUS is the National Union of Students, the UK students' body

explanation.surface: Someone hurt while out on a bike with company and students had to walk instead.
explanation.walkthrough: Cycling HURT moves its T to the front, giving THUR. The definition is cryptic: a cothurnus was worn on the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A cothurnus was the high laced boot worn by actors in Greek tragedy, so it is a thing that went on a foot.

clue.text: Clip, if cross, around the ear finally: papa stops mum flipping!

indicators.note: these letters stop up the flipped word, plugging its gap like a stopper
flipping turns the word for mum back to front

parts.note: mum means mute, silent
a cross is the letter X
C, for circa, means around

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of each of the two words

parts.note: last letters of the and ear
P is papa in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A cross parent threatens a clip around the ear, and dad steps in to stop mum losing her temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes ER from the ends of the ear. 'flipping' turns MUTE into ETUM, and XCERP 'stops' it after its E. 'Clip around the ear' reads as a smack, but clip alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Excerptum is Latin for an extract, and a clip is a short excerpt taken from a film or recording.

clue.text: High priest thanks Muslims for securing flight

parts.note: ta is British slang for thanks

indicators.note: securing something means holding it fast inside, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: the Shia are one of the two main branches of Islam
on the lam means in flight from the law

explanation.surface: A senior cleric thanks a group of Muslims for booking him on a plane.
explanation.walkthrough: TA + SHI(LAM)A. 'Flight' looks like air travel but means escape.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tashi Lama, also called the Panchen Lama, is one of the two highest priests of Tibetan Buddhism.

clue.text: Six lots of this vital acid, including extra tablet, found in 1854

indicators.note: the number is the answer with one more letter added, so the extra letter is taken back out

parts.note: six lots of this make the year found at the end of the clue, 1854, so this is a sixth of it, 309, read aloud as three-o-nine
E is slang for an ecstasy tablet

explanation.surface: A scientific note: a vital acid in multiple doses, with an extra pill, was discovered in 1854.
explanation.walkthrough: Six lots of this are found in 1854, so this is 309, spoken as three-o-nine. 'including extra' says that spelling holds one letter more than the acid: the tablet, E.
explanation.definitionFit: Threonine is one of the essential amino acids the body cannot make, so it must come from food: vital in that sense.

clue.text: Clan leader's tattoo I note when rising

parts.note: ink is slang for a tattoo

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means reading from the bottom up

parts.note: taken as written
soh is the fifth note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A tribal chief's tattoo, the speaker notes, is getting raised.
explanation.walkthrough: INK + I SOH turned upwards, HOSI.
explanation.definitionFit: Inkhosi is the Zulu title for a chief, the hereditary leader of a clan or tribe.

clue.text: Top off evening tune, as the case demands

indicators.note: in a down clue the top is the first letter, and taking it off removes it

parts.note: a serenata is a serenade, music played in the evening

explanation.surface: A musician trims the start of a night-time song when circumstances require it.
explanation.definitionFit: E re nata is a Latin phrase meaning according to the circumstances, used for actions taken as needed.

clue.text: Fruit from tropical tree, one planted by designer of London park

indicators.note: planted beside something means set right next to it in the line

parts.note: John Nash laid out Regent's Park in London
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An exotic fruit tree has been planted by the man who designed a London park.
explanation.definitionFit: Nashi is the Asian pear, a crisp round fruit grown in warm parts of eastern Asia.

clue.text: Daily papers returning leaves from a ballot box?

indicators.note: leaves means goes out of, so these letters depart from the word for daily

parts.note: diurnal means daily

indicators.note: returning has the abbreviation for papers come back the other way

parts.note: ID, identity papers

explanation.surface: Someone reads a daily newspaper as pages blow out of a ballot box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns ID into DI, which 'leaves' DIURNAL. The question mark warns the definition is playful: an urn can serve as a box for votes.
explanation.definitionFit: Urnal is the adjective for an urn, and ballots were once cast into urns, so a ballot box can be one.

clue.text: Gorge on maple loaf, leaving odd pieces

indicators.note: leaving the odd ones behind means only the even-numbered characters are kept

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters

explanation.surface: Someone stuffs themselves on a maple-flavoured cake, leaving a few odd scraps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gorge' looks like the verb to stuff oneself, but it is a ravine.
explanation.definitionFit: A nalla is an Indian word for a ravine or watercourse, a deep narrow valley.

clue.text: Activities of Greek brigands, a thousand, with pronounced socialist principles?

parts.note: K stands for a thousand

indicators.note: pronounced means we hear the word spoken, not spelt

parts.note: leftism is the politics of the left

explanation.surface: Greek bandits number a thousand and loudly claim to be socialists.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that the sounds match but the spelling with PH does not.
explanation.definitionFit: Klephts were Greek mountain bandits who fought the Ottomans, and klephtism names their way of life.

clue.text: Fate which is often said to accompany pretentious artist

parts.words: which is often said to accompany pretentious
parts.note: moi, French for me, is the word often said in a pretentious manner
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A remark about a showy painter whose fate is always talked about.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue explains its own piece: MOI is the word often said, in mock French, by pretentious people.
explanation.definitionFit: Moira is the Greek personification of destiny, one's allotted portion, hence fate.

clue.text: Waterlilies after November died — hybrid going west

indicators.note: coming after means following on in the line

parts.note: N is November in the radio alphabet

indicators.note: in an across clue, going west means running right to left

parts.note: ob., for obiit, means died
a mule is a hybrid of a horse and a donkey

explanation.surface: The waterlilies died after November, and the hybrid variety was lost.
explanation.walkthrough: Going west is also slang for dying, which keeps the scene of a pond in decline.
explanation.definitionFit: Nelumbo is the genus of lotus plants, aquatic flowers often grouped with waterlilies.

clue.text: Half of farmland cold and mostly dry, landing fruit-eater with massive bill

indicators.note: only half the word is wanted, so the rest is dropped

parts.note: arable land is farmland under the plough

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last bit is used

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold
a synonym for dry

explanation.surface: A cold, arid stretch of farmland is where a big-billed fruit-eating bird comes down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a hefty invoice, but it is a beak.
explanation.definitionFit: The aracari is a small toucan of tropical America that eats fruit using its huge beak.

clue.text: Head cut deal perhaps involving primary requirement for kindergarten

indicators.note: involving has the tool's name take in the letter, holding it inside

parts.note: a saw cut deal, deal being pine timber, so saw is the past of see dressed as a cutting tool

indicators.note: primary means first, so only the opening letter of the next word is needed

parts.note: its first letter

explanation.surface: A head teacher slashes a deal concerning what a nursery class needs most.
explanation.walkthrough: Deal is softwood timber, which a saw cuts. 'primary requirement for' takes K from kindergarten, and 'involving' has SAW hold it.
explanation.definitionFit: Skaw is a dialect word for a headland or promontory, as in the Skaw at the northern tip of Denmark.

clue.text: Indian town turned poster out: "A dance ending early (at five)"

indicators.note: turned round means the whole string runs backwards
finishing before the usual end means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: an ad is a poster
out means away from home
taken as written
the jive is a lively dance

explanation.surface: A town notice advertises a dance that will end early, at five o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: JIVE stops at V, the Roman five, which is the aside's joke. The whole of AD AWAY A JIV then reads backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Vijayawada is a large city in Andhra Pradesh in south-east India, on the Krishna river.
